# SwiGLU prefill, generated by stream-dse

`(SiLU(x @ w_gate.T) * (x @ w_up.T)) @ w_down.T` over `(seq_len, embedding_dim)` rows,
with `(out, in)` weights, as `nn.Linear` holds them. Its design is not written here:
[stream-dse](https://github.com/KULeuven-MICAS/stream) partitions the block into
fused groups, places every layer, and generates each group's design.

```python
from iron.operators.swiglu_prefill_stream.graph import SwiGLUPrefillStream

ffn = SwiGLUPrefillStream(w_gate, w_up, w_down)
y = ffn(x)
```

## What stream-dse is given and what it returns

| | Source |
|---|---|
| Workload | `design.swiglu_module()`, a `torch.nn.Module`, exported to ONNX (`iron/common/stream/workload.py`) |
| Candidate mappings | `design.candidates`: per partition and GEMM block, a `StreamMapping` of each layer's kernel arguments and the fused groups |
| Kernels | mlir-aie's `aie.iron.kernels` factories, described in `iron/common/stream/kernels/aie2p.toml` |

`select_mapping` prices every candidate by its solve and the dispatches between
its groups, and the cheapest is built. Each fused group's design comes back as
MLIR with the kernels it calls (`final.mlir`, `kernels.json`), and is a
`StreamOperator` (`iron/common/stream/operator.py`) whose `exported_design()`
returns it. The solve is cached under `$NPU_CACHE_HOME/stream/`.

## Partitions

| `partition` | Groups | Operators |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `gate, up, silu, mul, down` | `SwiGLUFusedStream` |
| 2 | `gate, silu, up, mul` and `down` | `SwiGLUGatedStream`, `SwiGLUProjectionStream` (down) |
| 5 | one per layer | `SwiGLUProjectionStream` (gate, up, down), `SwiGLUSiLUStream`, `SwiGLUMulStream` |

In partition 2 the SiLU and the product are post-ops: they run on the cores
of the gate and up GEMMs, on each output tile as its sum completes.

`SwiGLUPrefillStream` is the graph over them: a step per group of the
partition stream-dse chooses, which the full ELF dispatches in turn.
`partition` and `gemm_block` narrow what it chooses between; left `None`, it
chooses.
A GEMM block is the `(sequence, embedding, hidden)` block the tile search
starts from.

`seq_len` must be a multiple of the array's rows and hold a block on each;
`embedding_dim` and `hidden_dim` multiples of their block times the column
split. A candidate that does not divide is left out (`design.refusal`), and a
size no candidate fits is refused by `compatible()`.

## Installing

```bash
pip install -r requirements_stream.txt   # Python 3.12 or later
stream-setup-aie
```

Without these the operators are unresolvable and their tests skip.
